slot.brief: Diagram of Young's double-slit setup with slit separation and screen distance marked; compute fringe width for the given wavelength, or the shift when the whole setup is immersed in a liquid.

stem: In a Young’s double-slit experiment, the arrangement is as shown in the figure. For light of wavelength $600$ nm, find the fringe width when the slit separation is $0.30$ mm and the screen is $1.5$ m away.
working:
$$\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}=\dfrac{(600\times10^{-9})(1.5)}{0.30\times10^{-3}}=3.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}=3\ \text{mm}$$

Independent check: Fringe width: β = λD/d = (600×10⁻⁹ m)(1.5 m)/(0.30×10⁻³ m) = 3×10⁻³ m = 3 mm.
solution:
The fringe width in Young’s double-slit experiment is $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.
$$\beta=\dfrac{(600\times10^{-9})(1.5)}{0.30\times10^{-3}}=3.0\times10^{-3}\,\text{m}=3\,\text{mm}$$

draft.stem: In a Young’s double-slit experiment, the arrangement is as shown in the figure. For light of wavelength $600$ nm, find the fringe width when the slit separation is $0.30$ mm and the screen is $1.5$ m away.

figure.description: Draw a schematic Young’s double-slit setup. Show two narrow horizontal slits, one above the other, labelled S₁ and S₂, with their vertical centre-to-centre separation marked d = 0.30 mm. To their right, draw a vertical screen parallel to the slit plane; mark the horizontal distance from the slit plane to the screen as D = 1.5 m. Draw the central axis horizontally from the midpoint between the slits to the screen, and label the wavelength of the incident light λ = 600 nm. Do not mark fringe locations or fringe width.

draft.distractor_notes: A: underestimates the result by a factor of three. B: uses an incorrect distance or unit conversion. D: overestimates the fringe width by a factor of two.
